Rute.et: From Middle High German ruote, from Old High German ruota, from Proto-Germanic *rōdō. Akin to Old Saxon rōda, compare Hunsrik Rut, Dutch roede and English rod and rood (“cross”).

Rutsche.et: From Middle High German rütsche, deverbal from rütschen.

rutschen.et: From an onomatopoeic Middle High German rutzen, rützen (whence also the obsolete form rütschen), with change of -tz- to -tsch- as also in fletschen. Perhaps related to Old High German rūtezzen. English rutch and rutsch derive from this term or its cognates in …
